study: PCI post-submission blinded-action and cross-policy certification v1
status: Post-submission follow-up; not evidence available at the original submission
analysis: Compare within-population/regime seed means after averaging the two matched evaluation episodes. Retain all five training seeds. Paired t intervals, descriptive percentile bootstrap, and exhaustive two-sided sign-flip sensitivity; Holm on 36 primary tests (3 populations x 3 regimes x 2 comparators x 2 endpoints). Fixed old checkpoints are exploratory, not 20-30 new training seeds. No test-driven tuning.
record_blinding: OS-random field openings for state and action; action domain 1004. Nonces are public and are not the blinding secret. Rules remain public.
timing: One sequential prover worker on at most six CPU cores; four backend permutations balanced exactly over 24 points in every full episode. Record shared-host load. Not comparable as controlled hardware speedup over old runs. Whole episode time includes all four sampled backends and postprocessing, not Groth16-only execution.
boundaries: Trusted state authority and executor; no sensor authentication or crash-persistent ledger.
No RWARE proofs or policy-inference proofs.
Disclosure views intentionally reveal witness data; do not combine them with the SNARK-only view in a privacy claim.
Private witness files are synthetic reproducibility artifacts, not auditor-visible inputs.
Negative tests and distinct commitments are functional evidence, not a general privacy theorem.
New circuit keys and costs cannot be attributed retrospectively to the original studies.
